brief: JPM Market Intelligence holds a Tactically Cautious / Neutral equity view into the September 16 FOMC. The view is not fundamentally based, since JPM sees above trend GDP and over 20% EPS growth in 26Q3 and 26Q4 as supportive. It rests instead on the 10Y approaching a new cycle high near 4.99%, credit spreads likely to widen on heavy issuance, and higher volatility if Warsh keeps communication opaque. Craig Cohen's work shows a 2 standard deviation rise in the 10Y, currently about 50-55bp against 21.7bp month to date, precedes negative monthly equity returns, which JPM reads as bond volatility mattering more than yield levels. OIS prices over 90% odds of a 25bp September hike, up from about 60% before Thursday's PPI. Feroli expects hikes in September and December, a 4.0-4.25% year end median dot and a 3.25% long run dot. Jay Barry sets out five Fed outcomes without attaching probabilities and stays neutral on duration. The desk stays bullish Tech and would buy the AI pullback dip. Oil rose about 9% last week, and the trading desk sees the Strait of Hormuz contested past the midterms with a retest of roughly $120/bbl likely.
